text: Then the place. Advised by the Admiralty's hydrographer on tides and currents, they chose the port of Huelva, on Spain's southern Atlantic coast. Spain was officially neutral. But Montagu knew that in Huelva there was a very active German agent, Adolf Clauss of the Abwehr, German military intelligence, with excellent contacts among Spanish officials.
